subject.title: [Bug]: Teams app removal/re-add retains prior DM session history

question: Should OpenClaw reset Teams sessions and cached conversation references for bot-visible app-removal lifecycle boundaries, with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100371 as the canonical fix and an explicit Teams-local clear-history limitation?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the remaining choice sets a privacy/session-retention boundary and decides which open patch should own the security-sensitive fix.

options.title: Land lifecycle-boundary fix
options.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100371 as the scoped fix for observable Teams app lifecycle events while documenting the clear-history limitation.

options.title: Require broader forget policy
options.body: Pause both pull requests until maintainers define a user-facing Teams forget/reset policy that also covers local clear-history expectations without lifecycle events.

options.title: Treat as platform limitation
options.body: Reject server-side session resets for these Teams flows and document that OpenClaw keeps history unless Teams emits an observable lifecycle boundary or the user explicitly resets.

recommendation.title: Land lifecycle-boundary fix
recommendation.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100371 as the scoped fix for observable Teams app lifecycle events while documenting the clear-history limitation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent adjacent ownership signal for Teams persisted state and privacy-sensitive conversation reference behavior.
